steps.text: We first prove that adding zero on the right is identity: for every natural number n, n + 0 = n. This requires a separate induction proof and we record it here as Lemma One.
Next we need to handle addition by successors on the left: m + suc n reduces to suc (m + n) for all natural numbers m and n. This also requires its own induction proof, recorded as Lemma Two.
We now argue by induction on the first argument n in the goal statement n + m ≡ m + n.
Base case: when n is zero, 0 + m reduces to m by definition, and by Lemma One we know that m + 0 equals m, so both sides are equal.

Inductive case: assume the hypothesis n + m = m + n holds for an arbitrary natural number k (where in our actual induction context this corresponds to fixing m and varying n). Then suc n + m reduces by Lemma Two to suc (n + m), which equals suc (m + n) directly, matching the right-hand side.
